power.why: Grid service in the Memphis area was not available at the scale and speed xAI wanted for its Colossus buildout, so the company bought a former Duke power plant site in Southaven in July 2025 and built its own generation next to the load.
power.duration: Temporary mobile turbines were run from August 1, 2025 under a state reading that treated them as exempt equipment usable for under twelve months. A July 30, 2026 agreement with the Mississippi Department of Environmental Quality set removal to begin in August 2026 and conclude by July 2027.
power.gas_supply: Natural gas fired. The specific pipeline arrangement is not stated in the records reviewed for this page.
power.technology: Simple cycle natural gas turbines. The permitted units are specified with selective catalytic reduction for nitrogen oxide control. The interim fleet included SMT-130, M35 and TM2500 mobile units across several generations.

profile.campus: xAI Southaven, Mississippi (MACROHARDRR data center and the Stanton Road turbine plant), adjoining the Colossus campus in Memphis
profile.address: 2400 Stateline Road West, Southaven, DeSoto County, MS 38671
profile.reading:
This building is not in Memphis. Its mapped footprint sits just south of the Tennessee and Mississippi state line, and the DeSoto County, Mississippi parcel layer returns it unambiguously as parcel 108515000 0000700, 48.60 acres, address 2400 Stateline Road West, in the Stateline Road Industrial Park, zoned M-1, owned by MZX TECH LLC with an owner mailing address of 1450 Page Mill Road, Palo Alto, California, recorded at deed book 1025 page 24710. Tulane Road addresses in Memphis have circulated for this building. Those belong to xAI's separate Colossus 2 site roughly a kilometer north and on the Tennessee side of the line. The municipality here is Southaven, in DeSoto County, Mississippi.

The State of Mississippi named the facility itself. In a January 8, 2026 announcement the governor's office said xAI would invest more than 20 billion dollars in Southaven, called it the largest economic development project in state history, and said the data center would be known as MACROHARDRR, that xAI had purchased and was retrofitting an existing building to house it, that the project would create hundreds of permanent jobs in DeSoto County, that operations were expected to begin in February 2026, and that on completion the company's computing power would approach 2 gigawatts. The Mississippi Development Authority approved xAI for its Data Center Incentive, a sales and use tax exemption on computing equipment and software, and the City of Southaven and DeSoto County are supporting the project through fee in lieu agreements. Property records show the affiliate MZX Tech LLC, formed May 16, 2025, bought this building on December 23, 2025. MZX Tech now holds four DeSoto County parcels totalling roughly 269 acres, all zoned M-1, including the 114.49 acre power plant tract at 2875 Stanton Road.

That power plant is the reason this address is contested. It is on site generation for the campus, not IT load and not a capacity figure, and the two must not be conflated. A notice of intent to sue filed February 13, 2026 for the NAACP counted 27 turbines rated at least 495 megawatts combined, listing 14 SMT-130 units, one M35, and twelve TM2500 units across three generations, and estimated potential annual emissions of 2,508 tons of nitrogen oxides, 236 tons of fine particulates, 837 tons of carbon monoxide and 25 tons of formaldehyde. It alleged the units were built and run from August 1, 2025 without preconstruction, operating, prevention of significant deterioration or hazardous air pollutant permits. The Mississippi Department of Environmental Quality had treated them as exempt temporary mobile equipment usable under twelve months. Those are an objector's allegations and a regulator's interpretation, not findings.

What regulators actually did: on March 10, 2026 the Mississippi Environmental Quality Permit Board voted unanimously to grant a permit for 41 turbines with emission control technology, dispersion modeling and monitoring conditions attached, after a February 17, 2026 hearing at which residents raised noise and air quality objections. The Southern Environmental Law Center appealed that decision on April 9, 2026. The NAACP filed a Clean Air Act suit against xAI and MZX Tech on April 14, 2026 in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Mississippi, case 3:26-cv-00074-MPM-JMV, and moved for a preliminary injunction on May 6, 2026, later amending to cite 57 operating turbines. On June 18, 2026 the Department of Justice moved to intervene on national security grounds. Under a July 30, 2026 agreement with the state, temporary turbines were to begin coming out in August 2026 and be gone by July 2027, with the 41 permitted units installed in their place. A preliminary injunction hearing set for August 24, 2026 was postponed. The matter is open.

profile.capacity_note: The megawatt and gigawatt figures around this site are generation, not load. onsite_generation_mw of 1200 is xAI's own stated rating for the gas turbine plant under construction on the adjoining MZX Tech parcel at 2875 Stanton Road, and the 495 megawatt figure in the February 2026 court filing is the combined rating of the 27 interim turbines then counted. Neither is an IT capacity. it_capacity_mw is absent because no operator statement or filing gives an IT load for this building. utility_power_mw is absent because no interconnection or service figure with a named utility has been published. The state's reference to computing power approaching 2 gigawatts on completion is a company projection quoted by an economic development agency, covering xAI's whole operation rather than this building.
profile.location_note: Corrected location. The DeSoto County, Mississippi parcel layer returns this building's coordinates as parcel 108515000 0000700, 2400 Stateline Road West, owned by MZX TECH LLC, so the facility is in Southaven, DeSoto County, Mississippi, not in Memphis, Shelby County, Tennessee. The Tulane Road, Memphis addresses previously attached to this row lie roughly a kilometer north and on the Tennessee side of the state line, and belong to xAI's separate Colossus 2 building, which this registry tracks under its own entry.
profile.community_note: Southaven residents have objected mainly on noise and air quality. Neighbors reported turbine noise from November 2025, and a February 17, 2026 Mississippi Department of Environmental Quality hearing drew a large turnout at which no speaker supported the application. Residents have said their only reliable channel to the company runs through the mayor's office. xAI says it is spending millions of dollars on sound walls, silencers and next generation turbines, that its permitted units carry selective catalytic reduction, and that local air quality continues to meet or exceed federal standards. On the economic side the state describes more than 20 billion dollars of investment and hundreds of permanent jobs in DeSoto County, supported by a Mississippi Development Authority sales and use tax exemption and fee in lieu agreements with the city and county. On September 2, 2026 the Southaven Board of Aldermen approved a further 660,000 square foot xAI building at 8325 Tulane Road with conditions on streetscape, screening trees and perimeter fencing, alongside a 40 million dollar company contribution toward a police and fire training center.
profile.incentives_note: The Mississippi Development Authority certified xAI for its Data Center Incentive, which exempts computing and software equipment from sales and use tax. The City of Southaven and DeSoto County are supporting the project through fee in lieu of tax agreements. The governor's office put the total investment at more than 20 billion dollars and called it the largest economic development project in Mississippi history. Neither the term of the fee in lieu agreements nor the dollar value of the tax exemption is stated in the records reviewed for this page.
profile.regulatory_note: The permitting question is whether the turbines are stationary sources needing Clean Air Act permits or temporary mobile equipment that is exempt. The Mississippi Department of Environmental Quality took the exempt view for units run under twelve months, conditionally agreeing on July 29, 2025 and approving an exemption covering 18 turbines in August 2025. xAI applied on January 14, 2026 for a permit covering 41 turbines, and the Mississippi Environmental Quality Permit Board granted it unanimously on March 10, 2026 with control technology, modeling and monitoring conditions. That grant is under appeal by the Southern Environmental Law Center as of April 9, 2026. Separately, the NAACP suit filed April 14, 2026 in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Mississippi asks the court to hold that the interim turbines required preconstruction, prevention of significant deterioration and hazardous air pollutant permits. The Department of Justice moved to intervene for xAI on June 18, 2026, citing national security and testimony from the Defense Department's chief digital officer. No court ruling on the merits or on the preliminary injunction had issued when this page was written.
profile.campus_power_note: Generation for this campus sits on a separate MZX Tech parcel about a kilometer south of this building, the 114.49 acre tract at 2875 Stanton Road that was formerly a Duke power plant site and was bought by an xAI affiliate in July 2025. The same plant supplies xAI's Colossus 2 building at 5400 Tulane Road in Memphis, on the Tennessee side of the state line, which this registry tracks separately. Because the generation and the two data center buildings straddle the Tennessee and Mississippi border, the load sits in two jurisdictions while the air permitting sits entirely with Mississippi.
profile.onsite_generation_type: Natural gas turbines. 41 permanent units are permitted, replacing temporary mobile turbines that are being phased out.

profile.onsite_generation_status: Under construction as of xAI's July 30, 2026 statement. Temporary mobile turbines were operating in the interim, with removal to begin August 2026 and finish by July 2027.

reading.body:
This building sits in Southaven, Mississippi, just south of the state line, on a 48.6-acre parcel in the Stateline Road Industrial Park zoned for manufacturing. xAI's affiliate MZX Tech LLC bought it in December 2025 and retrofitted it as a data center. No operator statement or filing has published an IT load figure for the building, so its computing capacity is unknown. The governor's office projected that xAI's operations here would approach 2 gigawatts of computing power on completion, but that covers the whole company operation, not this campus alone.

Power comes from a 1.2-gigawatt natural gas generation plant under construction on an adjoining 114-acre former Duke power plant site at 2875 Stanton Road, also owned by MZX Tech, about a kilometer south and also in Mississippi. Forty-one permitted turbines with selective catalytic reduction for emissions control are being installed to replace temporary mobile units that ran from August 2025 under a state exemption for equipment usable under twelve months. The temporary removal and permanent unit installation schedule was set for August 2026 through July 2027 under a July 30, 2026 agreement with the Mississippi Department of Environmental Quality. The specific arrangement for natural gas supply has not been published.

The permit for the 41 permanent turbines was granted unanimously by the Mississippi Environmental Quality Permit Board on March 10, 2026 after a February 17, 2026 hearing where Southaven residents raised objections on noise and air quality. The Southern Environmental Law Center appealed that permit on April 9, 2026. The NAACP filed a federal Clean Air Act suit on April 14, 2026 in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Mississippi, alleging the interim turbines needed preconstruction and hazard permits they did not have, and moved for a preliminary injunction on May 6, 2026. The Department of Justice moved to intervene on national security grounds on June 18, 2026. No ruling on the merits or preliminary injunction had issued at the time of this writing, and the matter remains open.
